import pytest
from tablefmt import render


class TestJapaneseCharacterWidth:
    """Test that Japanese and other wide characters are handled correctly."""

    def test_japanese_names_basic_alignment(self):
        """Columns should line up when cells contain Japanese text."""
        result = render(
            [
                ["レポート_2024.pdf", 12, "2024-11-02"],
                ["notes.txt", 3, "2024-11-20"],
                ["議事録.docx", 48, "2024-10-15"],
            ],
            ["name", "KB", "modified"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Check that all data rows have the same length (visual alignment)
        # and that separators are at the same visual positions
        assert len(lines) > 0
        # Header line should exist
        assert "|" in lines[0]
        # Rule line should have consistent separators
        assert "-+-" in lines[1]
        # All data lines should have same number and position of separators
        separator_positions = []
        for line in lines[2:]:
            positions = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            separator_positions.append(positions)
        # All rows should have separators at the same positions
        if separator_positions:
            first = separator_positions[0]
            for positions in separator_positions[1:]:
                assert positions == first

    def test_single_japanese_cell_width(self):
        """Column width should accommodate full visual width of Japanese text."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート", "x"], ["abc", "y"]],
            ["name", "col"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Both data rows should have separators at the same column position
        positions_1 = [i for i, c in enumerate(lines[2]) if c == "|"]
        positions_2 = [i for i, c in enumerate(lines[3]) if c == "|"]
        assert positions_1 == positions_2

    def test_japanese_header_alignment(self):
        """Headers with Japanese text should align columns properly."""
        result = render(
            [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]],
            ["レポート", "col"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Separators in header and data should align
        header_seps = [i for i, c in enumerate(lines[0]) if c == "|"]
        data_seps = [i for i, c in enumerate(lines[2]) if c == "|"]
        assert header_seps == data_seps

    def test_japanese_with_mixed_width(self):
        """Table with both wide and narrow characters should align."""
        result = render(
            [
                ["日本語", "123"],
                ["abc", "456"],
                ["中文テキスト", "789"],
            ],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # All rows should have separators at the same visual position
        for line in lines:
            if "|" in line:
                sep_pos = line.index("|")
                # Verify the separator is at a consistent position
                assert sep_pos > 0

    def test_truncate_with_japanese_max_width(self):
        """Text truncation with max_width should respect visual width."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート_2024_ファイル.pdf", "x"]],
            max_width=10,
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # First data line should not exceed max_width in visual display
        # (this is a visual check - the string may contain Japanese that takes more space)
        assert "…" in lines[0] or len(lines[0]) <= 20  # rough check

    def test_wrap_with_japanese_max_width(self):
        """Text wrapping with max_width should work with Japanese text."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート ファイル もじ", "x"]],
            max_width=8,
            wrap=True,
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have multiple lines for wrapped content
        # At least the wrapped text should be present
        full_result = "\n".join(lines)
        assert "レポート" in full_result

    def test_right_align_with_japanese(self):
        """Right-aligned columns with Japanese text should work."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート", "123"], ["ab", "456"]],
            align="right",
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Verify separators align
        positions = []
        for line in lines:
            pos = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            positions.append(pos)
        if positions:
            for pos in positions[1:]:
                assert pos == positions[0]

    def test_center_align_with_japanese(self):
        """Center-aligned columns with Japanese text should work."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート", "x"], ["ab", "y"]],
            align="center",
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Verify separators align
        positions = []
        for line in lines:
            pos = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            positions.append(pos)
        if positions:
            for pos in positions[1:]:
                assert pos == positions[0]

    def test_mixed_alignment_with_japanese(self):
        """Mixed alignments with Japanese text should preserve column alignment."""
        result = render(
            [
                ["レポート", "123", "x"],
                ["notes", "456", "y"],
            ],
            align=["left", "right", "center"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Verify separators align in all rows
        all_positions = []
        for line in lines:
            pos = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            all_positions.append(pos)
        if all_positions:
            first = all_positions[0]
            for pos in all_positions[1:]:
                assert pos == first

    def test_emoji_width(self):
        """Emoji and other wide characters should be handled."""
        result = render(
            [["📄 file", "123"], ["document", "456"]],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Separators should align
        positions = []
        for line in lines:
            pos = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            positions.append(pos)
        if positions:
            for pos in positions[1:]:
                assert pos == positions[0]

    def test_combining_characters_width(self):
        """Combining marks should not affect layout (they don't add visual width)."""
        # e.g., "é" vs "e" + combining acute
        result = render(
            [["café", "123"], ["naïve", "456"]],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should still produce aligned columns
        assert len([l for l in lines if "|" in l]) >= 2

    def test_issue_example_exact(self):
        """Exact example from the issue report."""
        result = render(
            [
                ["レポート_2024.pdf", 12, "2024-11-02"],
                ["notes.txt", 3, "2024-11-20"],
                ["議事録.docx", 48, "2024-10-15"],
            ],
            ["name", "KB", "modified"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Verify that pipe characters are at the same visual positions across all lines
        pipe_positions = []
        for line in lines:
            positions = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            if positions:  # Only check lines with pipes
                pipe_positions.append(positions)
        
        # All rows should have pipes at the same positions
        if pipe_positions:
            expected = pipe_positions[0]
            for positions in pipe_positions:
                assert positions == expected, f"Pipes not aligned: {positions} != {expected}"

    def test_multiple_japanese_columns(self):
        """Multiple columns with Japanese text should all align."""
        result = render(
            [
                ["レポート", "ファイル", "日本語"],
                ["abc", "def", "text"],
                ["中", "文", "テキスト"],
            ],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # All separator positions should be consistent
        positions = []
        for line in lines:
            pos = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            positions.append(pos)
        if positions:
            first = positions[0]
            for pos in positions[1:]:
                assert pos == first

    def test_zero_width_joiner(self):
        """Zero-width joiners and similar should be handled."""
        # ZWJ emoji sequences like 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
        result = render([["test", "123"]])
        assert render([["test", "123"]]) == result

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "text,expected_visual_behavior",
        [
            ("a", "single_width"),
            ("あ", "double_width"),
            ("レポート", "all_double"),
            ("report_レポート", "mixed"),
            ("日本語テキスト", "all_double"),
        ],
    )
    def test_visual_width_consistency(self, text, expected_visual_behavior):
        """Various text types should maintain consistent column widths."""
        result = render([[text, "x"], ["ref", "y"]])
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Verify that separators stay aligned
        positions = []
        for line in lines:
            pos = [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            if pos:
                positions.append(pos)
        if positions:
            assert all(p == positions[0] for p in positions)

    def test_simple_japanese_no_headers(self):
        """Single Japanese cell should display correctly without headers."""
        result = render([["レポート", "x"]])
        # レポート has visual width 6 (3 chars × 2), x has width 1
        # First column should be 6 wide, second 1 wide
        lines = result.split("\n")
        assert len(lines) == 1
        # Visual alignment: レポート (6 chars) | x (1 char)
        # The separator should align properly
        assert "|" in lines[0]

    def test_japanese_with_ascii_mixed(self):
        """Mixed Japanese and ASCII in same column."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート_2024.pdf", "12"], ["notes.txt", "3"]],
            ["name", "KB"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # First row: header "name"
        # Second row: separator
        # Third row: レポート_2024.pdf
        # Fourth row: notes.txt
        assert len(lines) == 4
        # All rows should have separators at same column position
        sep_positions = [line.find("|") for line in lines]
        assert sep_positions[0] == sep_positions[1] == sep_positions[2] == sep_positions[3]

    def test_japanese_column_width_calculation(self):
        """Column width should account for display width of Japanese text."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート", "x"], ["ab", "yy"]],
            ["name", "KB"],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # レポート has visual width 6, "ab" has width 2, so column should be 6 wide
        # Find the separator position
        sep_pos = lines[0].find("|")
        # Everything before the | on each line should be the same visual length
        for line in lines:
            if "|" in line:
                before_sep = line[:sep_pos]
                # Visual alignment requires this to be properly padded
                assert before_sep.endswith(" ") or not " " in before_sep

    def test_truncate_with_japanese(self):
        """max_width truncation should account for display width."""
        # レポート (visual width 6) + _2024.pdf (visual width 8) = 14 total
        # With max_width=10, should truncate properly considering visual width
        result = render([["レポート_2024.pdf", "x"]], max_width=10)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # The cell should be truncated and end with … (1 visual width)
        # The result should fit within the visual width constraint
        assert len(lines) == 1

    def test_truncate_respects_visual_width_limit(self):
        """Truncated text should not exceed max_width visually."""
        result = render([["レポート_2024.pdf"]], max_width=8)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # The cell should be truncated to fit max_width of 8
        # e.g., レポート… would be 6 + 1 = 7 visual width
        assert len(lines) == 1
        truncated_cell = lines[0].strip()
        # Should end with ellipsis
        assert truncated_cell.endswith("…")

    def test_wrap_with_japanese(self):
        """Wrapping should account for visual width."""
        # Test wrapping Japanese text
        text = "レポート_2024_ファイル.pdf"  # Long text with multiple words
        result = render([[text, "x"]], max_width=8, wrap=True)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should be wrapped into multiple lines
        # Each line of the first column should be <= 8 visual width
        for line in lines:
            if "|" in line:
                cell = line.split("|")[0].rstrip()
                # Cell should not exceed max_width visually (accounting for spaces)
                # We can't easily verify visual width here, but we can check it wrapped
                pass
        # Should have more than 1 line due to wrapping
        assert len(lines) > 1 or "レポート_2024_ファイル.pdf" in result

    def test_mixed_width_columns_alignment(self):
        """Multiple columns with mixed ASCII/Japanese should align."""
        rows = [
            ["レポート_2024.pdf", "12", "2024-11-02"],
            ["notes.txt", "3", "2024-11-20"],
            ["議事録.docx", "48", "2024-10-15"],
        ]
        headers = ["name", "KB", "modified"]
        result = render(rows, headers)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        
        # Find separator positions
        sep_positions = []
        for line in lines:
            first_sep = line.find("|")
            second_sep = line.find("|", first_sep + 1) if first_sep >= 0 else -1
            if first_sep >= 0 and second_sep >= 0:
                sep_positions.append((first_sep, second_sep))
        
        # All separator positions should be consistent
        if len(sep_positions) > 1:
            first_seps = [sp[0] for sp in sep_positions]
            second_seps = [sp[1] for sp in sep_positions]
            # All first separators should be at same column
            assert len(set(first_seps)) == 1, f"First separator positions vary: {first_seps}"
            # All second separators should be at same column  
            assert len(set(second_seps)) == 1, f"Second separator positions vary: {second_seps}"

    def test_kanji_no_padding_overlap(self):
        """Padding should not cause column overlap with wide characters."""
        result = render(
            [["こんにちは", "a"], ["x", "world"]],
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Both rows should have separators at the same position
        positions = [line.find("|") for line in lines]
        assert positions[0] == positions[1]

    def test_emoji_handling(self):

        # Positions should be at the same column
        assert positions[0] == positions[1]

        """Combining marks with Japanese characters should work."""
        result = render([["レポート", "x"]])
        lines = result.split("\n")
        assert len(lines) == 1
        assert "|" in lines[0]

        """Right alignment should work with Japanese characters."""
        result = render([["レポート", "x"]], align="right")
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Both cells should have visual width, right alignment should pad on left
        assert len(lines) == 1

    def test_center_align_with_japanese(self):
        """Center alignment should work with Japanese characters."""
        result = render([["レポート", "xy"]], align="center")
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Both cells should be centered based on display width
        assert len(lines) == 1

    def test_header_with_japanese(self):
        """Headers with Japanese should align properly."""
        result = render(
            [["ファイル", "12"]],
            ["名前", "KB"],

        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Header line, separator line, data line
        assert len(lines) == 3
        # Separators should be at same position
        header_sep = lines[0].find("|")
        sep_line_sep = lines[1].find("|")
        data_sep = lines[2].find("|")
        assert header_sep == sep_line_sep == data_sep

    def test_long_japanese_name_truncate_max_width(self):
        """Long Japanese name with max_width should truncate correctly."""
        # 長いファイル名 is 7 characters with visual width 14
        result = render(
            [["長いファイル名_2024_01_15_backup.zip", "2048"]],
            max_width=12,
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have one line (or two if wrapping happened)
        truncated_line = lines[0]
        # Should end with ellipsis
        assert "…" in truncated_line or len(lines) > 1

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "text,expected_lines",
        [
            ("レポート", 1),  # 6 visual width, fits in max_width=10
            ("レポート_ファイル", 1),  # ~12 visual width, might need wrapping at smaller max_width
        ],
    )
    def test_japanese_truncate_parametrized(self, text, expected_lines):
        """Parametrized test for Japanese truncation."""
        result = render([[text]], max_width=10)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Basic sanity check

"""Tests for handling wide characters (Japanese, etc.) in table rendering."""

import pytest
from tablefmt import render


class TestJapaneseBasicAlignment:
    """Japanese text should align columns properly by display width."""

    def test_simple_japanese_alignment(self):
        """Single Japanese character column should align properly."""
        result = render([["あ", "b"], ["cd", "e"]], ["col1", "col2"])
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # col1 should be 2 columns wide (あ is display-width 2)
        # col2 should be 1 column wide (b, c, d, e are all 1)
        # But the actual column widths in the table need to match
        assert len(lines) == 3  # header, separator, data rows
        # All lines should have the same pipe positions
        header = lines[0]
        sep = lines[1]
        # Separators should mark column boundaries
        assert "-+-" in sep

    def test_japanese_mixed_ascii(self):
        """Column with mixed Japanese and ASCII should size correctly."""
        result = render([["レポート", "x"], ["abc", "y"]], ["name", "KB"])
        # レポート is 4 characters but display-width 8
        # abc is 3 characters and display-width 3
        # Column should be sized to accommodate the wider "レポート"
        lines = result.split("\n")
        assert len(lines) == 3
        # Verify columns align (all | should be at same position in each line)
        pipe_positions = [line.find("|") for line in lines]
        assert len(set(pipe_positions)) == 1  # All pipes at same position

    def test_japanese_in_header_alignment(self):
        """Japanese characters in header should affect column width."""
        result = render([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]], ["あいうえお", "col2"])
        # Header has Japanese (5 chars = 10 display-width)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        assert len(lines) == 3
        # Column 1 should be wide enough for the header
        assert "|" in lines[0]


class TestJapaneseTruncation:
    """Japanese text should truncate correctly when max_width is used."""

    def test_truncate_japanese_basic(self):
        """Truncating Japanese text should respect display width, not char count."""
        # レポート = 4 chars, 8 display-width
        # With max_width=5, should truncate to fit 5 columns including ellipsis
        result = render([["レポート", "x"]], max_width=5)
        # The first column should be truncated to ~4 display-width + 1 for ellipsis = 5
        # In characters, that's レ=2cols, ポ=2cols, ×(ellipsis)=1 = 5 cols
        # But we can only fit 2 chars (4 cols) + ellipsis (1 col) = 5 cols
        # So it should be "レポ…"
        assert "…" in result

    def test_truncate_japanese_exact_fit(self):
        """Japanese text that fits exactly should not be truncated."""
        # あ = 1 char, 2 display-width
        result = render([["あ", "x"]], max_width=2)
        assert "…" not in result
        assert "あ" in result

    def test_truncate_japanese_over_width(self):
        """Japanese text wider than max_width should be truncated."""
        # あいう = 3 chars, 6 display-width
        # With max_width=4, should fit 4 columns
        # あい = 4 columns, so "あい…" (4+1=5 is too much)
        # So "あ…" (2+1=3) or "あい" (4)? Since max_width=4 and ellipsis is needed,
        # we need to fit in 4 total. So we can have 3 columns + 1 for ellipsis = 4.
        # That's just "あ…"
        result = render([["あいう", "x"]], max_width=4)
        assert "…" in result

    def test_truncate_mixed_ascii_japanese(self):
        """Mixed ASCII and Japanese should truncate correctly."""
        # "a" = 1 col, "b" = 1 col, "レ" = 2 cols, "ポ" = 2 cols
        # "abレポ" = 6 columns
        # With max_width=5, should truncate to fit 5
        result = render([["abレポ", "x"]], max_width=5)
        # Can fit "ab" (2) + "レ" (2) = 4 columns, then + "…" (1) = 5
        assert "…" in result

    def test_truncate_japanese_min_width(self):
        """Japanese text with min max_width should work."""
        # Even with max_width=2, should work (but might just show ellipsis)
        result = render([["レポート", "x"]], max_width=2)
        # With max_width=2, we can only fit "…" (1) but need 2 chars minimum
        # So we might get "…" or some truncation
        assert len(result) > 0  # Just verify it doesn't crash


class TestJapaneseWrapping:
    """Japanese text should wrap correctly when wrap=True."""

    def test_wrap_japanese_basic(self):
        """Japanese text should wrap to fit max_width."""
        # "あいうえお" = 5 chars, 10 display-width
        # With max_width=4, should wrap to multiple lines
        result = render([["あいうえお", "x"]], max_width=4, wrap=True)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have multiple lines for the first column
        # Without wrapping we'd have 1 line, so wrap should create more
        assert len(lines) >= 2

    def test_wrap_mixed_text(self):
        """Mixed ASCII and Japanese should wrap correctly."""
        # "a b レポート" = word-breaks at spaces, レポート is 4 chars = 8 display-width
        # With max_width=5, "a" (1), "b" (1) fit, but "レポート" (8) needs wrapping
        result = render([["a b レポート", "x"]], max_width=5, wrap=True)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have wrapped the long Japanese word
        assert len(lines) >= 2

    def test_wrap_japanese_space_separated(self):
        """Japanese text with spaces should wrap at word boundaries."""
        # "word レポート more" with max_width=7
        result = render([["word レポート more", "x"]], max_width=7, wrap=True)
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should preserve space-separated words
        assert len(lines) >= 2


class TestJapaneseAlignment:
    """Japanese text should align correctly (left, right, center)."""

    def test_right_align_japanese(self):
        """Japanese text should right-align properly."""
        # Column width will be determined by width of text, then padded
        result = render([["あ", "bbbbb"]], align="right")
        # First column: あ (2 display-width) should be right-aligned
        # Second column: bbbbb (5 display-width) should be right-aligned
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Verify the pipes align
        assert lines[0].find("|") == lines[1].find("|")

    def test_center_align_japanese(self):
        """Japanese text should center properly."""
        # With odd/even padding, center should put extra space on right
        result = render([["あ"]], align="center")
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have some output
        assert len(lines) > 0

    def test_left_align_japanese(self):
        """Japanese text should left-align properly."""
        result = render([["あ", "bbbbb"]], align="left")
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Pipes should align vertically
        assert lines[0].find("|") == lines[1].find("|")

    def test_mixed_alignment_with_japanese(self):
        """Different alignments in columns with Japanese should work."""
        result = render(
            [["レポート", 123, "text"]],
            align=["left", "right", "center"]
        )
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have pipes at consistent positions
        assert "|" in lines[0]


class TestJapaneseUserCase:
    """Test the original user-reported case."""

    def test_user_reported_case(self):
        """Files with Japanese names should align columns properly."""
        result = render([
            ["レポート_2024.pdf", 12, "2024-11-02"],
            ["notes.txt", 3, "2024-11-20"],
            ["議事録.docx", 48, "2024-10-15"],
        ], ["name", "KB", "modified"])
        
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have header + separator + 3 data rows
        assert len(lines) == 5
        
        # All lines should have pipes at the same positions (column alignment)
        # Find all pipe positions in each line
        pipe_positions_per_line = [
            [i for i, c in enumerate(line) if c == "|"]
            for line in lines
        ]
        
        # All lines should have pipes at same positions (allow separator to have -)
        # For header and data rows, pipes should be at same positions
        assert pipe_positions_per_line[0] == pipe_positions_per_line[2]  # header == first data row
        assert pipe_positions_per_line[0] == pipe_positions_per_line[3]  # header == second data row
        assert pipe_positions_per_line[0] == pipe_positions_per_line[4]  # header == third data row

    def test_user_case_with_max_width(self):
        """User case with max_width should truncate Japanese correctly."""
        result = render([
            ["レポート_2024.pdf", 12],
            ["notes.txt", 3],
        ], ["name", "KB"], max_width=10)
        
        lines = result.split("\n")
        # Should have header + separator + 2 data rows
        assert len(lines) == 4
        
        # First row should have truncated name or be properly formatted
        # Pipes should align
        assert lines[0].find("|") == lines[2].find("|")
        assert lines[0].find("|") == lines[3].find("|")
